model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): net income to common less CET1 retention, net debt zero

historical_growth.core_revenue_note: Total operating revenue 3-yr (FY2022 restated 14,542bn -> FY2025 17,755bn) and 5-yr (FY2020 12,895bn) CAGRs are inflated by the IFRS 17 presentation change in 2023 and by FVTPL trading gains (2,409bn in FY2025 vs 1,211bn in FY2024). The core series NII + net fees (kpis): FY2020 12,266bn -> FY2022 13,010bn -> FY2025 14,616bn = 3.95% 3-yr, 3.6% 5-yr, which is the organic growth the base case is anchored on. NIM has compressed 2.08% (FY2022) -> 1.73% (FY2025) while the balance sheet grew.
historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is profit attributable to equity holders of the parent (already after the cash-settled PS charge): FY2020 3,414,595; FY2021 4,019,254; FY2022 4,665,643; FY2023 4,368,035; FY2024 4,450,177; FY2025 4,971,561. 5-yr 7.8% is from the FY2020 COVID-provisioning / NIM-trough year; 3-yr 2.1% is from the FY2022 NIM peak. EPS (after hybrid coupons) FY2020 6,654 -> FY2022 8,498 -> FY2025 9,812. Common equity ex-hybrids FY2020 41,890bn -> FY2022 46,535bn -> FY2025 53,209bn.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (3.5% FY2027-29 tapering to 2.5%), anchored on the core NII + fee CAGRs of 3.6-4.0%; the total-revenue CAGRs (6.6-6.9%) are not used because they carry the IFRS 17 change and trading gains, and the equity CAGR (4.9%) is depressed by buybacks (count 500m -> 486m) and the 51% payout, so it understates earnings power rather than measuring it.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5-yr CAGR 8.1% exceeds common-equity 5-yr CAGR 4.9% by >30%: the gap is the buyback-for-cancellation programme (shares 500.3m FY2020 -> 486.5m weighted FY2025) and a rising payout ratio, not faster compounding of the book. Total-revenue CAGRs (6.6-6.9%) exceed equity by >30% because of the IFRS 17 presentation change and trading gains. Growth is taken from the core NII + fee series and management's Value-Up targets, not from any of these.

scenario_narratives.base: Shinhan stays what it is: a top-2 Korean universal bank earning ~10.5% on regulatory capital and ~9.5% on common book, with revenue growing ~3% (household lending capped, corporate and overseas mid-single digits, NIM drifting down from the 2026 spread widening), the pre-tax margin reverting from the FY2026E cyclical high of 38.5% to a 36% mid-cycle by FY2030, and the Value-Up plan distributing ~70% of earnings through dividends and buybacks-for-cancellation while CET1 is held at ~13.4%. The axes are the BoK rate path versus NIM, household/real-estate credit costs, how much of the 2025-26 trading windfall repeats, and whether the 10% ROE target is met on common book or only on CET1.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Value-Up ROE target is met and held on common book: overseas profit compounds toward 30% of the group (Vietnam, Japan), securities and WM capture the household shift into capital markets, AI transformation takes cost-to-income under 40%, credit cost stays ~40bp, and the 38% margin proves to be the new normal rather than a peak. Faster balance-sheet growth consumes more retained capital, so the bull is driven by margin and payout more than by growth, and a re-rating toward 1.2x book follows a sustained double-digit ROE.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Korean household-debt cycle turns: the BoK cuts into a housing downturn, NIM compresses toward 1.55% as in 2020, real-estate PF and SME credit costs double, card merchant fees are cut again, the equity-market trading gains of 2025-26 reverse, and digital banks keep taking retail share. Revenue is flat for two years and the pre-tax margin falls to 32%, below the FY2023-24 trough, with ROE on common ~7.5% -- below the cost of equity -- and the FSC leaning on payouts. The balance sheet (CET1 13.4%, NPL 0.57%) means this is an earnings-and-multiple bear, not a solvency one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank earning roughly its cost of equity is worth roughly its book, and the model says so: Shinhan's FCFE to common (net income less the capital retained to grow CET1 inside the 13-14% range) discounted at a 9.5% KRW cost of equity values the common at about 1.0-1.1x common book across the weighted scenarios, against an ADR at ~0.94x book and ~9-10x FY2026E earnings. The upside case is not growth -- growth consumes capital at ~11% ROCET1 -- but the durability of the 2026 margin and the Value-Up distribution of the surplus CET1; the downside is the Korean household-debt cycle and the BoK, which the 25% bear weight prices. Hybrid coupons and NCI are charged inside the flow, SBC is cash-settled and inside G&A, and deposits and wholesale funding are operating liabilities, not net debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY0 is an estimate: the H1 2026 6-K is not extracted, so FY2026E revenue (+5%) and margin (38.5%) rest on the Analysis JSON's Q2 2026 facts; re-base when the filing lands
Cyclical peak anchoring: if 36% is still too generous a mid-cycle margin (FY2023-24 were 33.9%), base value falls ~KRW 6,500/share per margin point
KRW/USD: every USD value moves one-for-one with the won; a 10% won depreciation is -10% on the ADR regardless of the business
Hybrid bonds charged at coupon inside the flow, not at par in the bridge: the par treatment would take ~USD 7.5/share off every scenario
Share count assumes the FY2026 cancellation programmes complete as announced (~470m); treasury-share cancellation is now mandatory under the March 2026 Commercial Code amendment
Regulatory intervention (merchant-fee cuts, directed lending, payout guidance in a downturn) is in the bear path and the 25% weight, not in the base
Cost of equity 9.5% in KRW: each 50bp is ~KRW 8,000/share on the base value

sanity_check_note: scripts/sanity_check.py reads inputs.fx_rate as quote -> model (USD -> KRW), the reciprocal of the engine convention used here (see memory note sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict, CM and GGB precedents), so its historical price-to-book / P/E anchors for this KRW-model, USD-quote ticker will be off by the squared rate and any P/B or P/E trip or pass it prints should be re-derived by hand. KRW-consistent multiples at the 2026-10-02 Seoul close of KRW 104,800 (055550.KS, which ties to the ADR at parity): P/common book = 104,800 / 111,513 (53,209,435m / 477.16m) = 0.94x; P/E trailing = 104,800 / 9,812 = 10.7x; P/E FY2026E = 104,800 / ~11,220 (5,275,000m / 470m) = 9.3x; dividend yield on FY2025 DPS 2,590 = 2.5% plus ~2.5% of buybacks. Historical P/B band for Korean bank holdcos 0.4-0.7x (2015-2024) was itself the discount the Value-Up programme exists to close; 0.94x is the top of the ten-year range, not a mis-stated ratio.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SHG) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 47.05-85.57 USD. KRW/USD from Yahoo KRW=X and the Seoul listing 055550.KS at the same date for the parity check in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: SEC Form 20-F FY2016-FY2025 (research/SHG/Extracted/SHG_Annual_FY*.txt): consolidated statements of comprehensive income (FY2025 lines 60380-60418), financial position, changes in equity (hybrid coupons line 60572, treasury stock lines 60576-60577), cash flows (lines 60700-60707); capital adequacy table (CET1 and RWA lines 64250-64255); share count note (lines 27, 58818, 71880-71902); share-based payments note 43 (lines 71501-71550). Metrics CSV research/SHG/Reports/SHG_Metrics.csv (core_metrics + kpis: NIM, NPL, NII, fees, hybrid bonds, TotalCommonEquity, dividends, buybacks).
data_sources.qualitative: research/SHG/Reports/SHG_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): Q2 2026 results, Value-Up +++ targets (10%+ ROE, 50%+ return ratio, 13%+ CET1), FY2026 buyback programmes, overseas strategy, bull/bear axes.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total operating revenue in millions of KRW = net interest income + net fees and commissions + net insurance income less insurance finance expense + dividend, trading (FVTPL), FX and disposal gains, i.e. the 20-F 'Operating income' line grossed back up for the provision for credit losses, general and administrative expenses and other operating expenses, net. FY2025 actual (20-F F-8): 7,023,357 + 2,002,965 + 6,402,500 + 2,325,993 = 17,754,815. FY2024 16,654,408; FY2023 16,427,420 (IFRS 17 basis); FY2022 restated 14,542,000; FY2021 14,161,000; FY2020 12,895,000. FY2026E = FY2025 x 1.05: no H1 2026 filing is extracted, so the FY0 estimate rests on the Analysis JSON's Q2 2026 facts (net income ~KRW 1,820bn, +18% YoY; ROE 12.4%; record overseas profit) and the sector-wide widening of loan-deposit spreads after the mid-2026 household-lending curbs. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027 one year from the valuation date, as the engine's end-of-year discounting requires; the CSV has no Revenue column for this ticker and the CSV OperatingCashFlow/FreeCashFlow are loan/deposit movements, not used.
inputs.share_count_basis: Ordinary shares issued 485,494,934 at 31 Dec 2025 (20-F FY2025 note 43, line 27) less 8,337,535 treasury shares held at that date (line 58818; the un-retired balance of the KRW 1,250bn FY2025 buyback, 900bn of which was cancelled in-year) = 477,157,399 outstanding. LESS the FY2026 buyback-for-cancellation programmes: KRW 500bn approved 5 Feb 2026 (up to ~5.5m shares; 2,723,039 already acquired by the Feb 2026 dividend record date) assumed complete at ~5.3m shares, plus an ESTIMATED ~2.0m shares of the additional ~KRW 700bn tranche (~6.7m shares) announced after Q2 2026 and still executing = ~470m at the valuation date. The March 2026 Korean Commercial Code amendment mandates cancellation of all treasury shares, so acquired = cancelled. No dilutive instruments: performance shares are cash-settled, stock options ceased in 2010 with none exercisable (line 58791), hybrid bonds are non-convertible AT1. Held FLAT: the buyback is a distribution of the FCFE the model capitalises, not a separate source of value. REFRESH from the H1 2026 6-K / FY2026 20-F cover: if the full 700bn tranche is complete the count is ~465m (+1% to every per-share value).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. Shinhan is an FSC-regulated bank holding company: deposits KRW 447.6tn, borrowings and debt securities issued KRW 148.4tn (CSV TotalDebt) are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income, and cash and due from banks KRW 35.3tn is held against that funding and is not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to common equity (net income to common less capital retained to grow CET1 with risk-weighted assets at the 13-14% management range) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only. Hybrid bonds (AT1, KRW 4,749,837m at 31 Dec 2025, coupons KRW 197,932m in FY2025) and non-controlling interests (KRW 2,413,052m; profit share KRW 112,958m) are charged INSIDE the flow by taking the margin on a to-common basis (see margin_rationale), so neither is deducted again in an equity bridge. Memo: deducting the hybrids at par instead would take ~KRW 10,100/share (~USD 7.5) off every scenario; the coupon-in-flow treatment is the FCFE convention (USB precedent) and is the less conservative of the two.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE to common = net income to common ~5,275,000 (18,640,000 revenue x 38.5% pre-tax-to-common margin x (1 - 26.5%)) LESS capital retained ~1,960,000 (~4% RWA growth x ~KRW 49.0tn CET1 capital: CET1 47,115,338 at 31 Dec 2025 on RWA 352,907,638 = 13.35%, provisional 13.43% at Q2 2026). Implied FY2026E profit attributable ~5,485,000 (+10% on FY2025 4,971,561) after adding back ~210,000 of hybrid coupons; cross-check against Q2 2026 +18% YoY with the usual weak, one-off-laden Q4. Distributions cross-check: FY2025 dividends 1,293,828 + buybacks 1,250,001 = 2,543,829 = 51% of attributable profit (the Value-Up '50%+' ratio) while CET1 rose 13.0% -> 13.35%; the ~60% FCFE/NI ratio here is what the 13-14% CET1 range permits once the ratio sits inside it.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Equal to last_fcf: there is no share-based compensation to strip (see sbc_source) and no interest income to strip (see interest_income_note). Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 9,730,881; FY2023 529,846; FY2020 -4,409,317) is loan/deposit/trading movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV OperatingCashFlow and CapEx columns are not used.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero by substance, not by omission. Shinhan's only equity compensation plan is a performance-share (PS) scheme of CASH-settled virtual shares (20-F FY2025 note 43: 'Type: Cash-settled share-based payment'); the FY2025 charge of KRW 106,142m (CSV StockBasedComp; 41,874 FY2023, 46,636 FY2024, inflated in 2025 by the year-end share price) is a cash expense already inside general and administrative expenses, so it is inside the modelled margin and there is nothing to add back or dilute. Stock options ceased in April 2010. House and street bases therefore coincide and band_position is null.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income (KRW 27.99tn gross, 11.69tn net in FY2025) IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: Acquisition of treasury stock KRW 1,250,001m in FY2025 (cash-flow statement line 60703; 700,000 FY2024, 485,947 FY2023), all for cancellation. FY2026 programmes total ~KRW 1,200bn (500bn Feb 2026 + ~700bn mid-2026). The flat share count is funded by actual repurchases; buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in KRW (20-F, 'in millions of won'); the NYSE ADR (1 ADR = 1 ordinary share, no ratio) quotes in USD. fx_rate is the engine convention model -> quote: 1 / 1342.51 USD per KRW = 0.000744866, from Yahoo KRW=X at 2026-10-02T21:18Z. Parity check against the Seoul listing 055550.KS: ADR close x 1342.51 = KRW 104,756 vs KRX close KRW 104,800 on 2026-10-02 (0.04% apart), which proves the rate, the direction and the 1:1 ADR ratio in one line. All per-share values are computed in KRW and converted at this rate; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are USD so they are comparable to current_price, and the _krw twins are the model-currency values. The rate is dated and will rot: refresh_price.py moves the ADR price but never the rate. NOTE scripts/sanity_check.py reads fx_rate in the opposite direction (quote -> model); see sanity_check_note.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z NYSE regular close (Friday; valuation date is the following Saturday, no after-hours print involved)
inputs.share_count_date: 2025-12-31 (20-F count) adjusted for the announced FY2026 cancellation programmes; see share_count_basis
inputs.book_value_anchor: Equity attributable to equity holders KRW 57,959,272m at 31 Dec 2025 includes hybrid bonds 4,749,837m; common equity ex-hybrids 53,209,435m (kpis TotalCommonEquity) = KRW 111,513 per outstanding share (477.16m) = ~USD 83.1 at the fx rate, so the ADR trades at ~0.94x common book. CET1 capital 47,115,338m is the binding regulatory base (13.35% of RWA) and is what the retention driver grows; FY2025 return on common equity 4,773,629 / avg 52,331,535 = 9.1%, return on CET1 ~10.4%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in KRW, the currency of the flows: 10-year Korea Treasury Bond ~3.2% (yields rose through H2 2025 per the 20-F outlook; BoK on hold) + beta 1.1 x Korea equity risk premium 5.7% (mature-market 4.5% + ~1.2% country premium) = 9.5%. One rate across all three scenarios; rate-cycle, household-debt credit-cost and regulatory-intervention risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium. A USD-built rate would be wrong by the KRW-USD rate differential.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities KRW 790,339m (line 70842) against KRW 60tn of equity are immaterial; lease depreciation and interest sit inside G&A / interest expense and therefore inside the modelled margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction (one treatment: operating cost).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the flow: the margin driver is pre-tax income to COMMON = profit before tax less the pre-tax equivalent of NCI profit share and hybrid-bond coupons, so FY0 modelled net income ties to EPS x shares (FY2025: 4,773,629 to common = 9,812 x 486.5m). NCI equity and hybrid bonds are NOT deducted in an equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, net_debt = 0 (house precedent for banks: HBAN, USB, WFC, TFC, NTRS, STT, NAB.AX, BMO, RY). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = g x CET1 is the clean-surplus equivalent (value = CET1 + PV of returns above the cost of equity, expressed as distributable cash), and it runs through the validated slider engine which also produces the workbook. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF). Engine mapping: revenue = total operating revenue (see base_revenue_definition); 'ebitda' = pre-tax income to common = profit before income taxes less (NCI share + hybrid coupons)/(1 - tax), as % of revenue -- FY2023 33.9%, FY2024 33.9%, FY2025 36.6% (6,929,009 - (112,958 + 197,932)/0.734 = 6,505,400 / 17,754,815), FY2026E 38.5%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation KRW 1.30tn is inside G&A and is a genuine cost for a bank); sbc_pct = 0 (cash-settled PS plan already in G&A); 'capex' = capital retained to hold CET1 inside the 13-14% range as RWA grows = (CET1 / revenue ~2.63) x g/(1+g); cash_tax_rate = 26.5% (FY2025 effective 26.6%, FY2024 24.4%, FY2023 24.9%; Korean statutory 24% national + 2.4% local at the top bracket, Pillar Two top-up noted in note 46); wacc = cost of equity 9.5% in KRW; wc_capture 0. CYCLICALITY: FY2025-26 margins are the high side of the Korean rate/credit cycle (lending-curb spreads, equity-market trading gains, benign 0.57% NPL); the base reverts to a 36% mid-cycle margin by FY2030 rather than extrapolating FY2026E. Residual-income cross-check: P/CET1 = (ROCET1 - g)/(CoE - g) = (10.6 - 2.5)/(9.5 - 2.5) = 1.16x on ~KRW 49tn FY2026E CET1 = ~KRW 56.7tn = ~KRW 120,600/share, which the base engine value should approximate. Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) is unreported; 31 Dec 2025 is the latest extracted balance sheet and the H1 2026 6-K is NOT in Extracted/ -- the FY2026E anchors should be re-based when it is.

bear.growth_rationale: BoK resumes cutting into a housing/household-debt downturn: NIM compresses toward 1.55% (as in 2020), household loan books shrink under the FSC caps, card merchant fees are cut again, trading gains reverse as the equity rally unwinds, and digital banks (KakaoBank, Toss, K bank) keep taking retail share. Revenue flat for two years, then 2% nominal.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cost doubles to ~80bp (real-estate PF, SME, card receivables) in FY2028-29 while NIM falls, taking the pre-tax-to-common margin to 32% -- below the FY2023-24 trough of 33.9% -- before settling at 34% as provisions normalise but the lower-rate NIM does not fully recover. Government-directed 'relief' lending and contribution demands keep other operating expenses elevated. Implied FY2029 net income to common ~4,500bn, ROE on common ~7.5%, below the cost of equity.
bear.capex_rationale: 2.63 x g/(1+g) retention at the low growth path (1.0% -> 2.6%, 2.0% -> 5.2%) PLUS a 1pp CET1-conservation buffer in FY2027-29 (the FSC would lean on payouts in a credit downturn). Low growth means low retention and a high payout, which is the economically correct offset to the lower margin and why the bear value does not collapse: a slow-growing bank distributes most of what it earns.

base.growth_rationale: Total operating revenue. FY2027 3.5%: household lending growth capped by the FSC quotas (~2-3%), corporate/SME and overseas (Vietnam, Japan, US) mid-single digits, NIM flat-to-slightly-down from the 2026 spread widening as BoK stays accommodative, fees +4-5% (cards flat on merchant-fee cuts, securities/WM growing), insurance CSM release stable. Tapers to 2.5% terminal, below Korean nominal GDP (~3.5-4%) for digital-bank share loss and a mature, high-household-debt market. Brackets the core NII + fee CAGR of 3.6-4.0%.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income to common on revenue. FY2026E anchor 38.5% is the high side of the cycle (lending-curb spreads, 2,400bn+ trading gains on the 2025-26 equity rally, 0.57% NPL, cost-to-income 41.5%). Base reverts to 36.0% by FY2030 = mid-cycle: FY2023-24 were 33.9% with elevated PF/real-estate provisions (2.0-2.2tn), FY2025 36.6%; the 36% level assumes credit cost ~45bp (FY2025 ~40bp), cost-to-income drifting to ~42% as AX investment offsets branch rationalisation, trading income normalising to ~1.5tn, and the ~210bn/yr hybrid coupon plus ~120bn NCI charged inside. Implied FY2027 net income to common ~5,320bn (= 19,292bn x 37.5% x 0.735), ROE on common ~9.5%, ROCET1 ~10.6% -- i.e. the Value-Up '10%+ ROE' target is met on CET1 but only approached on common book.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at ~13.4% (inside the 13-14% management range) as RWA grows with revenue = (CET1 / revenue = 49.0tn / 18.64tn = 2.63) x g/(1+g): 3.5% growth -> 8.9% of revenue (~1,715bn FY2027, 32% of net income to common retained -> 68% distributed = ~1,350bn dividends + ~2,250bn buybacks, consistent with the 50%+ return ratio plus the surplus CET1 above 13%); 3.0% -> 7.7%; 2.5% terminal -> 6.4% (~25% retained, 75% distributed). Cross-check: FY2025 RWA grew 3.1% (342.4tn -> 352.9tn) and CET1 capital 2,553bn (5.7%), lifting the ratio 13.0% -> 13.35%; FY2024 RWA +9.0% was won-depreciation inflating FX-denominated assets.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 effective 26.6% (1,844,490 / 6,929,009), FY2024 24.4%, FY2023 24.9%; Korean corporate tax 24% national + 2.4% local at the top bracket = 26.4%, with Pillar Two top-up (note 46) and non-deductible items keeping the effective rate at or slightly above statutory.

bull.growth_rationale: Overseas earnings compound toward the 30%-of-profit 2030 target (Vietnam bank/finance/securities + Vingroup alliance, Japan with Mizuho/Rakuten), securities and WM ride the Korean capital-market reallocation, corporate lending offsets household caps, and NIM holds ~1.75% as the BoK stays on hold. Terminal 3.0% = Korean nominal GDP.
bull.margin_rationale: FY2026E's 38.5% proves durable: credit cost stays ~40bp, cost-to-income falls toward 39-40% on AI transformation (AX) and voluntary-retirement savings, trading/insurance income holds, and the Value-Up ROE target (10%+) is sustained on common book (ROE on common ~10.3%, ROCET1 ~11.5%).
bull.capex_rationale: Same 2.63 x g/(1+g) retention rule at the higher growth path: faster RWA growth consumes more capital (5.0% -> 12.5% of revenue), which is why the bull case is worth less per point of growth than a margin point -- the bank earns only ~11% on the capital it retains.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: the FY0 anchor is a cyclically strong year (lending-curb spreads, trading gains, benign credit) and the single most damaging error on a Korean bank is extrapolating a peak into a household-debt downturn; Korean banks also carry recurring regulatory intervention risk (merchant-fee cuts, directed lending, payout guidance) that is not in the base path. Bull cut to 25%: the ADR has already re-rated from the 52-week low (47.05) toward 0.94x book, and the bull needs margin durability, overseas execution and a sustained Korean equity-market reallocation all to hold at once, while faster growth consumes retained capital at only ~11% ROCET1.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
